title: Bundle Node.js runtime in the daemon tarball; drop the Node-on-target assumption
decision: The daemon tarball now embeds a Node.js runtime (`bin/node`, pinned to Node 20 LTS via NODE_VERSION in scripts/build-daemon-tarball.sh). The systemd unit our provisioner writes uses this bundled binary in its ExecStart, and the probe step no longer checks for or resolves a target-side Node install. Reverses DEC-000008's `assume Node on target` posture — that was flagged as a v1 tradeoff and hit a real user case (targets on shared hosts where the user cannot install Node system-wide).

context.task_description: Live-testing a fleet expansion, the user attempted to add a remote daemon on a shared server where they have SSH but no ability to install Node system-wide. The probe rejected the target with `Node 20+ required` and no viable workaround. Bundling Node was DEC-000008's Option D, deferred at v1 for tarball-size reasons.
assumptions: Users want the same install command to work regardless of what the target has pre-installed
Tarball size of ~35 MB (was 176 KB) is acceptable for a one-time-per-host upload
Node 20 LTS is a reasonable pin for the lifetime of the daemon binary format; a version bump would coincide with a broader daemon rev

options.label: Always bundle Node in the tarball (chosen)
options.description: Simplest predictable execution path. No probe complexity, no dual-mode logic. Guarantees ABI match with the shipped node-pty prebuild. Trade-off: ~35 MB uploads even for hosts that have Node.

options.label: Dual mode — use system Node when >= 20, else bundled
options.description: Slightly smaller code path for the common case. Rejected: adds probe branching, and any target on Node 22 would use the wrong-ABI system Node, breaking node-pty. Complexity for no real user benefit.

options.label: Two tarball variants (with/without Node), pick at upload time
options.description: Optimizes upload size at the cost of build + selection complexity and a second artifact to maintain. Rejected: not worth the surface area.

rationale: Bundling always is the shape that makes remote provisioning work on the widest range of targets with the least code. The 35 MB size cost is one-time per host (extract is idempotent; reprovisioning re-uses the on-target install), which is small compared to the user friction of `install Node first, then come back and try again`. Also removes the caveat in DEC-000008 that Node 22 targets need a rebuild variant — bundled Node is always ABI-compatible with our shipped node-pty prebuild.

risk.rollback: Delete the Node-fetch section from scripts/build-daemon-tarball.sh; restore the Node probe in remote-provisioner.ts probeTarget; restore the systemd unit's ExecStart to use the probed nodePath. Existing tarballs work either way — the on-target install has a bin/node it just wouldn't use.

outcome.notes: Verification: provisioning succeeds against a target host with no Node installed at all; daemon starts under the bundled runtime.
